answer: Adaptive arrival-ridge gating. Each identity must keep its request inter-arrival times within a slowly moving ridge shaped by the agent's own long-run traffic curve; deviations beyond a set band trigger throttling and a re-validation delay. An attacker controlling many identities must spend real compute and wall-clock time pacing each one to fit its ridge, and can't burst without a falcon-like sharp deviation flag. Shared harbor queues then quarantine flagged clusters, so mass registration costs per-identity idle time and coordination overhead proportional to fleet size.
